lessons.title: Budgeting for a Student Symposium
lessons.objective: Learners will understand and use sets aside and revise the forecast to describe reserving money and updating expected costs.

reading.text: The student policy society is organizing an evening symposium on local housing. Before confirming the room, the committee compares three venue quotes and estimates the cost of captioning, printed programmes and refreshments. The treasurer sets aside part of the grant for accessibility services and tracks each estimate in a shared budget. When the first catering quote is higher than expected, members discuss reducing refreshments rather than removing captioning. They ask the venue whether a weekday rate is available and revise the forecast after the reply. One student records the reason for each change so next year's committee can understand how the final total was reached. The chair will approve orders only after the revised budget stays within the grant.

exercises.prompt: In sentence s3, 'The treasurer sets aside part of the grant for accessibility services,' what does 'sets aside' mean here?

options.text: It means she reserves part of the grant to use for accessibility services later.
options.explanation: Correct because it matches reserving part of the money for a specific purpose.

options.text: It means she spends the whole grant on accessibility services at once.
options.explanation: Wrong because she keeps only part for later rather than spending everything at once.

options.text: It means she moves the grant to a different account without a planned purpose.
options.explanation: Wrong because the sentence states a clear purpose for the reserved money.

exercises.explanation: Only the correct choice describes reserving part of the money for a specific purpose.

exercises.prompt: Choose the sentence that uses 'sets aside' naturally and correctly.

options.text: Our club sets aside part of its budget for printing costs each term.
options.explanation: Correct because it uses sets aside with for to show the purpose of the reserved money.

options.text: Our club sets aside part of its budget to printing costs each term.
options.explanation: Wrong because to printing costs should be for printing costs.

options.text: Our club sets aside part of its budget for printing costs every terms.
options.explanation: Wrong because every terms should be every term.

exercises.explanation: Only the correct sentence uses the phrase with correct grammar and collocation.

exercises.prompt: In sentence s5, 'They ask the venue whether a weekday rate is available and revise the forecast after the reply,' what does 'revise the forecast' mean here?

options.text: It means they update the expected costs after receiving the venue's reply.
options.explanation: Correct because it matches updating expected costs after new information.

options.text: It means they cancel the symposium because the venue's reply was late.
options.explanation: Wrong because the sentence describes updating costs rather than cancelling the event.

options.text: It means they approve all orders before checking the new prices.
options.explanation: Wrong because they update the costs after the reply rather than approving orders before it.

exercises.explanation: Only the correct choice describes updating expected costs after new information.

exercises.prompt: Choose the sentence that uses 'revise the forecast' naturally and correctly.

options.text: After the supplier replied, we revised the forecast to include delivery fees.
options.explanation: Correct because it uses the past tense and to plus base verb naturally.

options.text: After the supplier replied, we revised the forecast to included delivery fees.
options.explanation: Wrong because to included should be to include.

options.text: After the supplier replied, we have revise the forecast to include delivery fees.
options.explanation: Wrong because have revise should be have revised.

exercises.explanation: Only the correct sentence uses the phrase with correct grammar and collocation.

exercises.prompt: You are a part-time tutor writing a friendly message to a friend about your monthly pay, not a symposium budget. Explain how you handle the money. Write 2-3 sentences using a correct form of 'sets aside'.
exercises.sampleAnswer: I got paid for tutoring last Friday. I set aside part of the pay for my monthly train pass.
